title: The Richest Houses With No Two Neighbours

concept.title: For every item decide: take it or skip it
body: Houses stand along a street, and every house holds some money. You may collect from any houses, but **never from two houses that stand next to each other** (the alarm would ring). What is the largest total you can collect? For `1 2 3 1` the best is houses 1 and 3 (1 + 3 = 4); for `2 7 9 3 1` it is 2 + 9 + 1 = 12.

Walk along the street and keep two numbers: `take` is the best total when the **current house is collected**, and `skip` is the best total when it is **not collected**. Moving to the next house `x`: if you take it, the previous house must be skipped, so the new `take = skip + x`; if you skip it, the previous house may be anything, so the new `skip = max(skip, take)`. The answer is `max(take, skip)` after the last house.

body.code:
take = skip = 0
for x in money:
    take, skip = skip + x, max(skip, take)
print(max(take, skip))

body: The two numbers are the whole **state** of the problem: all we need to know about the past is whether the last house was taken. Finding the right small state is the main skill in DP. The time is O(n), the memory O(1). The total can be as large as 2 * 10^14, so C++ and Java need 64-bit numbers.

statement: There are `n` houses in a row; the house `i` holds `money[i]`. You may collect the money of any set of houses in which no two houses are neighbours. Print the largest total you can collect.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the number of houses.
The second line has `n` numbers: the amount of money in each house, in the order along the street.
hints: After each house keep two values: the best total if this house is taken, and if it is not taken.
If you take the house, the previous one must have been skipped.
If you skip it, the previous one can be anything: take the larger of the two values.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
money = list(map(int, input().split()))

explanation: Two values are kept while walking along the street: the best total when the current house is taken (the previous one was skipped) and the best total when it is skipped (the larger of the two earlier values). The answer is the larger one after the last house.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
money = list(map(int, input().split()))

take = skip = 0
for x in money:
    take, skip = skip + x, max(skip, take)
print(max(take, skip))
